goal: Phase 0 of the lean campaign (docs/intent-factory/TECH-SPEC-2026-09-05-lean.md, revision 2): remove the three failure classes that cost the last campaign most of its nodes. Scope findings become advisory on completed attempts, review gains none|advisory|blocking modes with judge-protocol recovery that never degrades blocking silently, and resume retries nodes in place with explicit reconciliation and budget boundaries. Three chained autonomous nodes on the 0.2.0 runner from an immutable snapshot. Take 4: scope-advisory is implemented and uncommitted in the tree (three worker passes, verification green); the Sol judge left two majors on the non-green safeguards that this take fixes with maxRevisions 2, then review-modes and retry-in-place run.

definitionOfDone.text: A completed implementation attempt whose controller verification passed and whose worker changed a path outside its declared writeFiles/writeRoots proceeds to the gate and can reach done, with the unexpected paths recorded in node state under scopeFindings, a scope.finding event appended to events.jsonl, the paths listed in the judge prompt and a note in status; proven by a named test in scripts/runner.test.mjs.

When controller verification failed, the existing failure path is unchanged except that the unexpected paths are appended to the message; declared_paths_changed, the unknown-effect and result-materialization guards, and the ignore-source integrity check (snapshot_ignore_changed) behave exactly as before, shown by their existing tests still passing unmodified.
writeRoots accepts an existing regular file as a root that matches exactly that path, in validation and in the scope gate; proven by a named test.

taskPacket.objective: Make scope findings advisory on completed attempts. A worker whose controller verification passed is never failed for writing outside its declared scope: the unexpected paths become a recorded finding on the node, visible to the judge and in status, and the node proceeds to the gate. writeRoots may name files. Every other safeguard stays as it is.
instructions: Read docs/intent-factory/TECH-SPEC-2026-09-05-lean.md sections 1 (item 1), 3 (rule 1) and 5 before changing code. This node implements rule 1 for the 0.2.0 runner and nothing more.

Never start a command in the background or through a task tool, and never wait on one with a sleep loop: the harness denies background Bash and the controller reads silence as a stall. Run only the declared verification commands, in the foreground, with output bounded by | tail -n 200. Do not run the full npm test at all; the orchestrator runs it at phase close.

The implementation of this node already exists, uncommitted, in the tree (git status shows 12 files: runner.mjs, render.mjs, verification.mjs, contract.mjs, lib.mjs, task-packet.mjs, new scope-findings.mjs, runner.test.mjs, verification.test.mjs, contract.test.mjs, intent-settlement.test.mjs, helpers.mjs, references/contract.md) and its declared verification is green. Read git diff first. A judge left exactly two major findings, quoted verbatim; fix them and nothing else. (1) 'runner.mjs sets completedAttempt from envelope.status === "done" whenever no canonical-file parse error exists, without validating envelope.result. That enables deferViolation. A normal turn.completed carrying blocked_context or an invalid/missing worker result is only parsed later, where it becomes context_missing or an invalid-result repair without verification, a scope finding, or unexpected_write. The new incomplete-worker test covers turn.failed only, not this completed-envelope/non-accepted-result path.' Fix: a completed attempt is exactly an attempt whose canonical worker result file parses with status done; a done envelope without that file, a blocked_context result or an invalid file never defers the scope verdict and keeps the immediate terminal unexpected_write; add the named test for a done envelope whose result is blocked_context plus an unexpected write. (2) 'runner.mjs calls applyVerificationFailure first and invokes appendUnexpectedPathsToFailure only when TERMINAL.has(state.status). For a gated node with revisions remaining, applyRejection immediately starts the next worker; startWorker clears the prior error, verification, and scope. The unexpected paths are therefore lost rather than appended to the verification-failure message. The red-path test uses gate:false, so it exercises only the terminal branch.' Fix: record the unexpected paths into the verification-failure message and into the retry prompt's failure section before applyVerificationFailure runs, so both the terminal branch and the rejection-with-revisions branch carry them; add the named test with a gated node that has a revision remaining.

In skills/mine/intent-factory/scripts/runner.mjs, find the worker-phase scope evaluation that transitions a completed attempt to failed with error code unexpected_write after the worker's canonical result was accepted. Change only that path: when the controller's deterministic verification for the attempt passed, record the unexpected paths (bounded to 64 entries) in node state under scopeFindings, append an event of type scope.finding to events.jsonl, and continue into the gate exactly as a clean node would. When verification failed, keep the existing failure behaviour and only append the unexpected paths to the error message. If the current order evaluates scope before the controller runs verification, reorder those two steps for this path only.

Do not change declared_paths_changed, the unknown-effect reconciliation and result-materialization guards, or the ignore-source fingerprint that raises snapshot_ignore_changed; their existing tests must keep passing without modification. The workspace snapshot, its comparison and its five root exclusions (.runs, .git, node_modules, .claude, .codex) stay as they are.

Node snapshot validation in skills/mine/intent-factory/scripts/contract.mjs rejects unknown fields; extend it so scopeFindings (an object with an unexpectedPaths string array of at most 64 entries) is a valid optional node field, and cover it with a test.

Add a 'Scope findings' section to the judge prompt listing the unexpected paths when scopeFindings is present, so the judge can raise a finding about them. STATUS.md and status --json show a scope finding as the node note (for example 'scope: 2 unexpected paths'); see render.mjs.

In skills/mine/intent-factory/scripts/task-packet.mjs, validateWriteRoot must accept an existing regular file as a root in addition to a directory; a file root matches exactly that path in the scope gate. writeRoots stays allowed only in autonomous packets.

Tests: adjust the existing tests that assert a terminal unexpected_write on a completed attempt with green verification so they assert the advisory outcome instead; add named tests for the green-with-unexpected-path case (scopeFindings, event, judge prompt section), for the red-with-unexpected-path case (existing failure plus paths in the message), for the file writeRoot, and for scopeFindings snapshot validation. Use the replay driver or the fake providers the suite already uses; no sleeps.

Update skills/mine/intent-factory/references/contract.md ('Task packets' and 'What a gate costs, and what it will not see') in a few sentences so it describes the advisory scope. Do not touch SKILL.md.

Prefer a new module (for example skills/mine/intent-factory/scripts/scope-findings.mjs) over growing runner.mjs. From the worker, run only the declared verification commands with bounded output (they take under ten minutes); the orchestrator runs the full suite at phase close.

Do not modify campaign control artifacts under .runs/control or .runs/campaigns and do not commit. Writing the canonical result file the controller designates under .runs/<run>/results/ is required, and tests may create isolated temporary directories.
decisions: Scope is a review concern, never a terminal state on a completed attempt whose verification passed (TECH-SPEC lean, rule 1).
Ambiguous-effect, result-materialization and snapshot-integrity safeguards are out of scope and stay unchanged.
nonGoals: Do not change budget derivation, the judge verdict protocol, resume, or provider routing.
Do not remove or weaken the workspace snapshot, the scope comparison or the ignore-source fingerprint.

definitionOfDone.text: A gate object without review defaults to advisory: a fail verdict records its findings and an event, never re-dispatches the worker, and the node reaches done when verification passed; blocking keeps the failOn/maxRevisions behaviour; none skips the judge; validation rejects a blocking gate whose failOn omits major and any failOn that lists major without critical; each proven by a named test.

Verdict candidates are counted at the provider boundary: two separate agent-message verdicts, empty output, a missing terminal envelope and a timeout each trigger exactly one bounded re-ask; after a second failure an advisory node with green verification settles done with gate.verdict invalid_judge_output, while a blocking node transitions to blocked with error code judge_unavailable keeping its accepted worker result and verification records on disk exactly as a node awaiting its judge would, so that resume can re-judge it; proven by named tests for each shape.

A Definition-of-Done item may declare proof {kind: 'verification', ref: <index>} naming a verification entry by position; at gate time the recorded result of that entry (pass or fail and output) is reused instead of executing anything, while command proofs always execute and are never matched against verification argv strings; proven by a test that counts executions and by a validation test rejecting an out-of-range ref.

taskPacket.objective: Add review modes to the gate and make the judge protocol recoverable without ever degrading a blocking review silently: gate.review is none, advisory or blocking, defaulting to advisory; verdict candidates are counted at the provider boundary; one bounded re-ask, then advisory completes with invalid_judge_output while blocking enters attention with the work preserved; validation enforces failOn thresholds; a DoD command proof equal to a verification argv reuses the recorded result.
instructions: Read docs/intent-factory/TECH-SPEC-2026-09-05-lean.md sections 1 (items 2 and 11), 3 (rule 2 and 'Verification once per attempt') and 9 before changing code. This node implements rule 2 for the 0.2.0 runner.

Never start a command in the background or through a task tool, and never wait on one with a sleep loop: the harness denies background Bash and the controller reads silence as a stall. Run only the declared verification commands, in the foreground, with output bounded by | tail -n 200. Do not run the full npm test at all; the orchestrator runs it at phase close.

In skills/mine/intent-factory/scripts/contract.mjs, the gate object accepts a new field review with values none, advisory or blocking; omitted means advisory; gate: false is equivalent to none. Validation: a blocking gate whose failOn omits major fails with a message naming the node and the rule; any failOn that lists major without critical fails (the runner checks exact membership, so major alone lets critical through); advisory ignores failOn. Node snapshot validation must admit the new gate states (verdict invalid_judge_output, error code judge_unavailable) and any new field you add; it rejects unknown fields today.

In skills/mine/intent-factory/scripts/runner.mjs, the judge is dispatched only when review is not none and the node has judgment items (keep the existing conditional-judge logic). Advisory: a fail verdict records findings and maxSeverity in node state, appends an event of type gate.advisory, and the node settles done when its deterministic verification passed; it never consumes a revision or re-dispatches the worker. Blocking: current failOn and maxRevisions behaviour unchanged.

Judge protocol recovery. parseJudge alone cannot see the recorded phase-4 defect because skills/mine/intent-factory/scripts/drivers/exec-jsonl.mjs selects the last structured agent message before parsing. Count verdict-shaped candidates at the provider boundary (the codex normalization path) and expose the count in the envelope. Zero candidates (empty output), more than one candidate (two agent messages each carrying a verdict), a missing terminal envelope (incomplete_stream) and a judge timeout each trigger exactly one bounded re-ask, reusing the existing uncited-rejection re-ask machinery. When the re-ask fails again: advisory review settles the node done (verification passed) with gate.verdict invalid_judge_output and an attention note; blocking review transitions the node to blocked with error code judge_unavailable and leaves the accepted worker result, the verification records and the gate state on disk exactly as they are for a node awaiting its judge, so that the retry-in-place node can make resume re-judge it; never re-run the worker. Do not change resume in this node. Do not change how a single valid verdict is applied.

Proof reuse by reference only: add proof kind 'verification' whose ref is the zero-based index of an entry in the node's verification array; validation rejects an out-of-range ref; at gate time the recorded result of that verification entry for this attempt is reused (pass or fail and output) and nothing is executed. Command proofs keep executing exactly as today. Never compare a proof command string with a joined verification argv: a joined argv loses argument boundaries and shell semantics (printf %s 'value; false' exits 0 as argv and 1 as a shell string). Add a test that counts executions and a validation test for the out-of-range ref.
STATUS.md and status --json show 'advisory: N findings', 'judge: invalid output' or 'needs you: judge unavailable' as the node note where applicable (render.mjs).

Tests, each named after its case: default advisory; advisory fail verdict reaches done with findings and event; blocking unchanged; none skips the judge; validation rejects blocking without major and major without critical; two separate agent-message verdicts; empty judge output; missing terminal envelope; judge timeout; advisory settles invalid_judge_output; blocking enters judge_unavailable with work preserved; proof reuse counts one execution. Use the replay driver or the fake providers the suite already uses; no sleeps.
Update the 'Gates' and 'What a gate costs, and what it will not see' sections of skills/mine/intent-factory/references/contract.md in a few sentences. Do not touch SKILL.md.

Prefer a new module (for example skills/mine/intent-factory/scripts/review-modes.mjs) over growing runner.mjs. From the worker, run only the declared verification commands with bounded output; the orchestrator runs the full suite at phase close.

Do not modify campaign control artifacts under .runs/control or .runs/campaigns and do not commit. Writing the canonical result file the controller designates under .runs/<run>/results/ is required, and tests may create isolated temporary directories.
decisions: Deterministic verification is the gate; model review is advisory unless a node opts into blocking (TECH-SPEC lean, rule 2).
A judge protocol failure never fails a node whose verification passed, and never silently passes a blocking review: blocking becomes attention with the work preserved (TECH-SPEC lean, 9.1).
nonGoals: Do not change the worker result protocol, scope evaluation, resume, budgets or provider routing.
Do not change how a single valid verdict is applied in blocking mode.

definitionOfDone.text: resume adopts and re-judges completed work first: orphaned running nodes as today, and nodes blocked with judge_unavailable (accepted worker result and verification recorded, review unresolved) are re-judged with the gate's judge and never re-dispatched to a worker; then it re-dispatches failed, stalled, canceled, timeout-exhausted and dependency_failed nodes in the same run directory as attempt plus one whose prompt carries a 'Previous attempt' section (error, findings, scope findings, failing verification tail) bounded to 8 KiB; unknown_effect_reconciled is re-dispatched only with --reconcile <node>; an exhausted run budget is reported as attention and continued only with an explicit --max-input-tokens extension recorded in the run; --node <id> limits the retry to that node and its dependents; each proven by a named test on the replay driver.

resume accepts a working tree whose HEAD is a descendant of the recorded gitHead and records the new head, still refuses a non-descendant, and treats a dirtyTreeFingerprint mismatch as a status warning rather than a refusal; each proven by a named test.

contract prune, contract-prune.mjs, the targetedFix field and the single-node-contract warning are gone from code, tests and references; validate accepts a single-node contract silently; SKILL.md no longer lists contract prune and passes test/docs-diet.test.mjs.

taskPacket.objective: Retry in place: resume adopts completed work first, then re-dispatches ordinary failures as attempt plus one with the previous error and findings appended, in the same run directory, accepting a HEAD that descends from the recorded gitHead; unresolved effects need explicit reconciliation and an exhausted budget needs an explicit extension. contract prune and --targeted-fix are removed.
instructions: Read docs/intent-factory/TECH-SPEC-2026-09-05-lean.md sections 1 (item 4), 3 (rule 4) and 9 (decision 3) before changing code. This node implements rule 4 for the 0.2.0 runner.

Never start a command in the background or through a task tool, and never wait on one with a sleep loop: the harness denies background Bash and the controller reads silence as a stall. Run only the declared verification commands, in the foreground, with output bounded by | tail -n 200. Do not run the full npm test at all; the orchestrator runs it at phase close.

Recovery first, extended: keep the existing adoption of orphaned running nodes and the re-judge of finished work, and add one transition to that recovery path: a node blocked with error code judge_unavailable (introduced by the review-modes node: accepted worker result and verification records on disk, review unresolved) is re-judged by the gate's judge on resume and is never reset to pending or re-dispatched to a worker. Today recoverOrphan ignores blocked nodes and resume would reset them to pending; change that for this code only, with a test. Then, for nodes whose status is failed, stalled, canceled, exhausted by wall clock, or blocked with dependency_failed: return them to pending and dispatch them as attempt plus one (attempt is the worker-start counter; revisions, the gate-rejection counter, is not reset). A node blocked with dependency_failed becomes pending when the dependency it waited on is retried. --node <id> limits the retry to that node and the nodes that depend on it.

Stop boundaries. A node in unknown_effect_reconciled is re-dispatched only when resume is given --reconcile <node-id>, which records the acknowledgement in events.jsonl; without it resume lists the node as attention and leaves it. When the run's cumulative ledger budget is exhausted (search runner.mjs for budget_exceeded and the cumulative spend check), resume reports attention and exits non-zero unless --max-input-tokens <n> raises the contract-level ceiling; the extension is persisted in run.json with the previous value, the new value and a timestamp. Do not change budget derivation otherwise.

The regenerated worker prompt for a retried attempt appends a 'Previous attempt' section: error code and message, judge findings (severity and text), scope findings if present, and the failing verification commands with a bounded output tail; the whole section is bounded to 8 KiB. The judge prompt for that attempt receives the same section under the same heading.

Source identity on resume (search runner.mjs for 'source identity is incomplete; resume refused' and the gitHead comparison): accept a current HEAD that is a descendant of the recorded gitHead (git merge-base --is-ancestor <recorded> <current>) and record the new head in run.json; still refuse a non-descendant HEAD with the existing message. A dirtyTreeFingerprint mismatch becomes a warning surfaced in status, not a refusal, because workers and the orchestrator commit between attempts.

Remove contract prune: delete skills/mine/intent-factory/scripts/contract-prune.mjs, the 'contract prune' CLI branch, the targetedFix node field and its validation, the single-node-contract warning in validate, their tests, and their paragraphs in references/contract.md and references/release-1.md. A single-node contract is simply valid. Remove the 'Continue a partly finished run' row from SKILL.md and keep SKILL.md under the byte ceiling enforced by test/docs-diet.test.mjs.
Node snapshot validation in contract.mjs rejects unknown fields; extend it for any field you add (for example a reconciliation acknowledgement or a budget extension record) and cover it with a test.

Tests, each named after its case, using the replay driver or the existing fake providers: judge_unavailable node re-judged on resume without a worker dispatch; failed node retried as attempt 2 with the 'Previous attempt' section present and bounded; stalled and canceled nodes retried; dependency_failed node pending after its dependency is retried; --node targeting; unknown_effect_reconciled left alone without --reconcile and retried with it; exhausted budget reported as attention without --max-input-tokens and continued with it, extension persisted; descendant HEAD accepted and recorded; non-descendant HEAD refused; dirty fingerprint mismatch warns; contract prune CLI and targetedFix gone and a single-node contract validates without warning. No sleeps.
Update the 'Resume' section of skills/mine/intent-factory/references/contract.md and the 'Detached launch and waiting discipline' paragraph that mentions single-node contracts.

Prefer a new module (for example skills/mine/intent-factory/scripts/retry.mjs) over growing runner.mjs. From the worker, run only the declared verification commands with bounded output; the orchestrator runs the full suite at phase close.

Do not modify campaign control artifacts under .runs/control or .runs/campaigns and do not commit. Writing the canonical result file the controller designates under .runs/<run>/results/ is required, and tests may create isolated temporary directories.
decisions: A retry is the same run and the same node, attempt plus one, with the failure attached; instructions are frozen per run (TECH-SPEC lean, rule 4 and 9.3).
unknown_effect_reconciled and an exhausted budget are stop boundaries that only an explicit flag crosses.
nonGoals: Do not change scope evaluation, review modes, worktrees or provider routing.
Do not change the adoption of orphaned running nodes beyond adding the judge_unavailable re-judge transition.
